pairs.subject: observability-telemetry
pairs.evidence: src/lib/crash-history-db.ts:204 Imported UE crash logs are written to the crash_history table with truncation as the only transformation. No scrub runs between composition and the first write (a repo grep for redact/scrub/sanitiz over the crash analyzer, its route, store and DB found nothing), so user paths, machine facts and any secrets inside a pasted log persist in the shared SQLite file, which breaks the sanitize-before-persist one-way door.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/crash-history-db.ts:204 Bounding is done well: raw log capped at 64k chars with a marker, 200 frames, and the 200-signature cap is enforced by the writer (pruneCrashHistory() runs after every insert, line 237). Aggregation keys on a signature fingerprint, and reads are defensive (the parseJson fallback, line 135ff). The sanitize-before-persist gate is missing entirely: the raw log, error message, crash_dir and machine_json are stored as received.

src/components/modules/evaluator/CrashAnalyzerView/index.tsx:253 The in-product crash viewer (list plus per-record detail) reads the actual store: GET /api/crash-analyzer calls listCrashHistory (src/app/api/crash-analyzer/route.ts:25), and the viewer states the retention bound. Gaps: no export/copy-record action, and clearCrashHistory exists in the lib but has no UI management action.

pairs.registryProposal: crash-record-storage assumes the store holds the product's OWN crash evidence, written by a dying process. A crash-analysis tool that ingests a foreign program's crash logs (here, UE5 logs pasted into a dev tool) still needs sanitize-before-persist, bounds and defensive reads. The 'synchronous, one-file-per-record' write-path rules do not apply because the writer is healthy. The technique could state that split explicitly.
